children: Zellmer will succeed Hakan Samuelsson by October 2027 as Volvo navigates weaker EV demand, tariffs and rising development costs

Volvo Cars has named Klaus Zellmer, the current Chief Executive Officer of Volkswagen-owned Skoda, as its next President and CEO, setting out a leadership transition as the Swedish automaker works to revive sales and improve profitability amid challenging market conditions.

According to Reuters, Zellmer will assume the top role no later than 1 October 2027, succeeding Hakan Samuelsson, who returned as CEO in 2025 to help steer the company through a difficult operating environment.

The leadership transition comes as Volvo faces weaker electric vehicle demand, rising development costs and the impact of international tariffs, while also navigating changing conditions across key markets.
Zellmer brings more than 30 years of experience in the automotive industry to the role. He currently serves as CEO of Skoda, one of Volkswagen Group's key brands.
In a statement cited by Reuters, Volvo Cars Chairman Li Shufu said Zellmer had demonstrated an ability to guide organisations through periods of transformation and shifting market conditions.
His appointment establishes a longer-term succession plan for Volvo as the automaker works on a multi-year strategy focused on expanding its model line-up and strengthening its global position.
Volvo Cars, which is majority-owned by China's Geely Holding, has faced pressure from weaker EV demand, tariff-related challenges and elevated development spending, Reuters reported.

The company has also experienced slower sales in the United States and China, two important markets for the automaker. Its shares have fallen more than 45 per cent this year, Reuters reported, reflecting investor concerns around the company's growth prospects and market environment.
Volvo is also balancing its operations across Western and Chinese technology ecosystems while managing geopolitical and trade pressures affecting the automotive industry.

The leadership announcement follows Volvo's recent strategy day, where the company outlined plans to expand its product portfolio.According to Reuters, Samuelsson said Volvo intends to launch 13 new vehicles by 2030, with the broader strategy aimed at doubling the company's market share over the decade.

The company has also reported stronger-than-expected demand for its EX60 electric SUV, even as overall market conditions remain challenging.Volvo is adjusting its manufacturing footprint as part of its efforts to manage tariffs and strengthen supply chain flexibility. Production of the hybrid XC60 is being moved to South Carolina, while output of the EX30 is being increased at the company's Belgium facility.

Zellmer will take over as Volvo's leadership transition unfolds against a backdrop of changing consumer demand, increasing competition and continued uncertainty around the pace of electric vehicle adoption.
His appointment gives Volvo a defined succession timeline as the company pursues product expansion while responding to profitability pressures, tariffs and evolving market conditions.
